overview:
NJ-10 is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in New Jersey, with a partisan lean of roughly D+27. LaMonica McIver, who took the seat in a 2024 special election and won the general election that fall, is running for re-election. Her Republican opponent, Carmen Bucco, has raised under $10,000 and reports about $2,300 on hand, while McIver has raised more than $2.5 million and holds nearly $900,000 in cash. No outside groups are spending against her, and prediction markets put her chances near 97 percent.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and market pricing. With no expert ratings and no polling, some uncertainty remains, but the structural advantages in this seat make a Republican upset very unlikely.
